title: The Live Asset
premise: Beatrix Oyelaran, a whistle-blower living under four identities, works deniable cases from a network of safe houses — until her current one is listed online, its interior photographed down to the taped-over webcam and the false wall behind the bookshelf. Someone inside her handler chain has sold her location, and the listing itself is a message: we know everything, and we want what you buried. The secret is a ledger implicating the private intelligence firm that once employed her, and the buyer willing to pay in blood is the firm's founder — her former mentor and first love, Elias Vane. To survive, Beatrix must decide whether to destroy the ledger, sell it to a journalist, or use it as leverage to burn the network that abandoned her, all while the man sent to retrieve it is the only other person who ever knew her real name. In the end she trades the ledger's existence, not its contents — faking its delivery to trigger the firm's internal purge — and walks away with a new fifth name, chosen this time by herself.
about_author: Beatrix Montrose is the pen name of a former compliance investigator who spent a decade writing risk assessments for firms she no longer trusts. She writes thrillers from an undisclosed coastal town and answers to several names, only one of which is real.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Scrolling rental sites at 3 a.m., Beatrix finds her safe house listed with photos of its interior — including the false wall. She verifies the photos were taken nine days ago, while she was inside. The beat is cold dread: invisibility was a service she paid for, and the invoice has come due.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Debt
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix, with a flashback in Elias's voice. She inventory-loads her go-bag and recalls how her handler, Mercer, built the four-name system after her whistle-blowing nearly got her killed. She calls the emergency line; it rings to a disconnected number. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing your protectors were your captors.

chapters.title: The Man at the Open House
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Posing as a buyer at the listing's open house, Elias — now the firm's retrieval specialist — reads the staged rooms like a confession and finds Beatrix's hidden micro-recorder behind a radiator. He pockets it without reporting it. The beat is longing weaponized: duty and love pulling the same trigger finger.

chapters.title: Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Holed up in a Belfast hostel, she decrypts the ledger she's kept for six years: payments, disappearances, a senator's name. She drafts three exits — burn it, sell it, trade it — and realizes each requires trusting someone. Beat: the loneliness of a truth no one can be told safely.

chapters.title: Mercer's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Mercer. The handler meets Beatrix in a car park, admits the firm listed the safe house deliberately to flush her out, and offers her a new identity in exchange for the ledger — then warns her that Elias is the one they sent. Beat: betrayal with a human face; Mercer cries and means it.

chapters.title: What the Camera Saw
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Reviewing the micro-recorder's footage, Elias watches six-year-old recordings of himself and Beatrix — and one clip of the firm's founder ordering a death Beatrix witnessed. He must choose: deliver her, or become her accomplice. Beat: love re-lit as mutiny.

chapters.title: The Price of Quiet
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. A firm wet team finds her in Belfast; she survives by triggering a fire alarm and losing them in a hospital, but a bystander is hurt and her face hits local news. Beat: guilt and escalation — her secrecy has a body count, and the ledger starts to feel like a debt owed outward.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix and Elias, alternating. They meet at a coastal lighthouse, guns on the table, history between them. Elias offers the founder's own blackmail file as a counterweight; Beatrix proposes the trade: a fabricated ledger delivery that will make the firm devour itself. Beat: two people negotiating trust with ammunition.

chapters.title: The Handover
chapters.summary: POV Elias. In the founder's glass office, Elias delivers the forged ledger while Beatrix, on comms, feeds Mercer's evidence to a journalist on a dead-man's timer. The founder realizes mid-handshake that the numbers are wrong. Beat: the climax — power discovering it has been read like a document.

chapters.title: Fifth Name
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The firm purges itself; Mercer is arrested, Elias vanishes into his own four names, and the journalist sits on the real ledger as insurance. At a passport office in Lisbon, Beatrix fills in a fifth name — hers, chosen freely — and mails the true ledger to no address at all. Beat: bittersweet freedom; love deferred, self reclaimed.
